faq.a: Usman is associated with the Arabic form عُثْمَان, whose core sense is usman; young bustard.

faq.q: What is the origin of Usman?
faq.a: Usman is associated with Arabic. Usman is Arabic عُثْمَان (ʿUthmān), a lexical item for a young bustard. It was borne by the third caliph.
Yes — the underlying form عُثْمَان is Arabic.
Usman can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Usman should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿUthmān is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Usman mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Usman is rendered عثمان and carries the sense عثمان، پرندے کا بچہ.

faq.q: What does Usman mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Usman is rendered عثمان and carries the sense عثمان، جوجه هوبره.
A romanized syllable approximation is us-man. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Usman?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Usman, usman. Script forms are عثمان, عُثْمَان, उस्मान.

faq.q: Is Usman a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
